answer: A farm running 190 keys thus pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the wharf stake is held until the pigment settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the walnut audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 30% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
